title: Jev, an AI for making quick decisions, has been a viral hit in Silicon Valley. But OpenAI is hot on its heels
key_facts: TypeSafe AI released Jev in September; it classifies and sorts inputs (for example routing customer messages) at a fraction of the cost of leading models.
Per Vercel, nearly 13% of its paid teams tried Jev within a day of its arrival on Vercel's AI Gateway, more than twice any previous model launch in the first 24 hours.
Fortune says OpenAI launched a competing Decisions API on 6 Oct, built on the existing GPT-6 Luna model without further training.
OpenAI says its interface returns decisions up to ten times faster than calling GPT-6 Luna through the general Responses API; it accepts images, Jev accepts only text.
Input price: $0.10 per million tokens for OpenAI against $0.042 for Jev; neither charges for output tokens.
TypeSafe spent two years developing Jev and raised a $40 million seed round led by DCVC.
Developers still have to establish whether the judgments are accurate enough for their task; one developer found Jev let important emails slip through until he made his questions more specific.
quote_evidence: Vercel said Jev reached more than twice as many paid teams in its first 24 hours as any previous model launch.
Perhaps the clearest sign that TypeSafe was on to something: on Oct. 6, just three weeks after Jev’s launch, OpenAI rolled out a competing product, called Decisions API.
Developers still have to establish whether its judgments are accurate enough for their particular task.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheap, fast purpose-built models for routine sorting decisions are drawing a direct response from OpenAI.
event_date: September 2026 (Jev); 6 Oct 2026 (OpenAI Decisions API, per Fortune)
notes: Fortune's own reporting. Another outlet (Pasquale Pillitteri) headline dated 29 Sep says OpenAI launched Decisions API; Fortune says 6 Oct. Date taken from Fortune, attributed.
